questions.q: Which type of twins is more common?

options.e: Wrong. Conjoined twins are a rare variant of monozygotic twins.
Wrong. This is a membrane type, not a twin type.
Correct. Dizygotic twins make up about 70% of twins.

questions.q: What proportion of twins is dizygotic?

options.e: Wrong. This is the monozygotic proportion.

questions.q: What is the incidence of dizygotic twins per 1000 births?

options.e: Wrong. This is the monozygotic incidence.
Correct. Stated incidence for dizygotic twins.

questions.q: Dizygotic twins arise from how many ova and sperms?

options.e: Wrong. Each ovum needs its own sperm.
Correct. Two ova are fertilized by two sperms.

questions.q: Which set of features describes dizygotic twins?

options.t: Different appearance, same or different sex, 2 amnions, 2 chorions, 2 placentae
Different appearance, always the same sex, 1 placenta
options.e: Wrong. Sex may differ and placentae are two.
Wrong. Appearance differs and sex can differ only in dizygotic twins.

questions.q: Which twin type is always of the same sex and looks identical?

options.e: Wrong. Appearance differs and sex can differ.
Correct. One ovum and one sperm give identical twins.
Wrong. Fraternal is another name for dizygotic.
Wrong. This is dizygotic and may differ.

questions.q: What is the incidence of monozygotic twins per 1000 births?
A monozygotic twin pregnancy has 2 placentae, 2 chorions and 2 amnions. When did separation occur?

options.t: At or before the morula stage
options.e: Correct. Early separation gives dichorionic diamnionic twins.
Wrong. This gives 1 placenta, 1 chorion, 2 amnions.
Wrong. This gives 1 placenta, 1 chorion, 1 amnion.
Wrong. Late separation leads to conjoined twins.

questions.q: Separation at the blastula stage gives which membranes?

options.e: Wrong. This follows separation at or before the morula.
Wrong. This follows separation at the germ disc.

questions.q: Separation at the germ disc stage gives which membranes?

options.e: Wrong. This is the blastula stage.
Wrong. This is at or before the morula.

questions.q: Which is the correct order from earliest to latest stage of monozygotic separation?

options.e: Wrong. The morula precedes the blastula.
Wrong. The blastula precedes the germ disc.

questions.q: What proportion of premature babies are twins?

options.e: Wrong. This is the single-pregnancy perinatal mortality.
Correct. About 12% of premature babies are twins.
Wrong. This is the proportion of twin pregnancies delivering two infants.

questions.q: What is the perinatal mortality in twins compared with singletons?

options.e: Wrong. Not the stated twin value.

questions.q: What proportion of women pregnant with twins give birth to two infants?

options.e: Correct. Only 29% do, due to losses such as vanishing twin.

questions.q: One twin dies in the 1st or early 2nd trimester and is completely absorbed. What is this called?

options.e: Wrong. The dead fetus is compressed, not absorbed.
Correct. The healthy single pregnancy continues.

questions.q: A twin dies in the 2nd trimester and is crushed and flattened between the membranes. What is this called?

options.e: Correct. The dead twin is mummified while the survivor enlarges.
Wrong. The vanishing twin is absorbed.
Wrong. This is conjoined twins at the head.
Wrong. This is conjoined twins back to back.

questions.q: What is the cause of conjoined twins?

options.t: Incomplete separation of the germ disc
options.e: Correct. They occur in monozygotic twins.

questions.q: Conjoined twins fused at the head are called?

options.e: Wrong. Not listed in the lecture.

questions.q: Conjoined twins fused at the thorax are called?

options.e: Wrong. Not listed in the lecture.

questions.q: Conjoined twins fused back to back at the buttocks are called?

options.e: Wrong. Not listed in the lecture.
